newsitem.title: FRANCE: China says problems over, Chirac to visit Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China says problems over, Chirac to visit Beijing.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Saturday that tensions between China and France over French arms sales to Taiwan were over and President Jacques Chirac would visit Beijing in May.
Asked after meeting Chirac at the Elysee Palace whether relations were now stable after recurrent problems over the sale of French ships and combat aircraft to Taiwan, Qian replied: "I believe so."
A spokeswoman for Chirac later said the French president would pay a state visit to China lasting four or five days in mid-May.
She quoted Qian as telling Chirac: "This visit will be a remarkable event in Franco-Chinese relations."
Chirac's visit will be preceded by separate visits to China in the coming weeks by at least four French ministers and the president will be accompanied on his visit by a large group of businessmen.
Qian arrived in Paris on Friday night for talks with Chirac and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette and with French business leaders.

Chirac's spokeswoman, Catherine Colonna, later told reporters the French president had brought up the issue of human rights during the talks on which China has been regularly at odds with Western nations.

A diplomatic clash over the subject clouded the visit to Paris of Chinese Premier Li Peng in April 1995 when speeches due to be given at an official dinner were not pronounced when it was realised that they would directly contradict each other over human rights.
Colonna quoted Chirac as saying the European Union wanted to hold a dialogue with China over the subject which would be preferable to continued disagreement and confrontation.
She said Qian told Chirac that China was ready for dialogue with both human rights groups and with judicial experts about human rights.
Qian was also quoted as saying China was studying the possible ratification of two United Nations pacts on human rights.
Colonna said the two men discussed economic cooperation at length and that Chirac asked that all countries be treated equally by China in its foreign economic exchanges.

The statement was understood to mean France still resented punitive measures taken by China against Paris at the time of the signing of arms contracts with Taiwan which were not levelled against the United States which also sold arms to Taiwan at the time.
